critical.claim: Most individual relationship studies favored higher Mediterranean-diet adherence; four of five studies examining relationships reported favorable associations
critical.source_says: 9 studies were included... 5 studies reported an impact of MedDiet on athletic performance; of these, 4 studies reported a positive effect. ... The other studies showed no effect (i.e., 4 of 9 positive, and the 5 impact studies [25,27-29,31] are not the 5 cross-sectional studies)

minor.issue: Says eligible performance outcomes were pooled but omits that only 3 studies (2 RCTs, 1 longitudinal) fed the meta-analysis.
Omits that all studies came from Spain or Italy and that most studies were at high risk of bias, mainly from how outcomes were measured.
Volume/issue 35(11) cannot be verified from the source (in-press xxx); the article number 104165 is correct.
Advice on carbohydrate, protein distribution, timing and the food list is general sports-nutrition guidance rather than findings of this review.

'Body composition could be pooled from only one study' is imprecise: the source says only one article was available for some body-composition measures (ECW, ICW, BCM, SMM), while fat mass was pooled and showed heterogeneity.

note: B accurately reports the 5-of-9 impact (4 positive) and the null pooled SMD with the correct design and bias details; A overstates the share of favorable individual studies by misframing the denominator as 4 of 5 relationship studies.
